dashboard.title: Help — Dashboard

actions.label: Overview
actions.text: The dashboard shows counts of locations, units, open issues and open tasks. Click a card to go to the related screen.

actions.label: Print briefing
actions.text: Opens a printable overview of open tasks per team — useful on the shop floor.

actions.label: Trial period
actions.text: During the trial you have extended limits. The dashboard shows remaining days.

actions.label: Add issue
actions.text: Create an issue in two steps: location/unit + description, then a task for the right team.

dashboard.status_note: Issue status on the dashboard follows the status of linked tasks.

statuses.new: At least one task has not been started yet.
statuses.in_progress: At least one task is in progress.
statuses.done: All tasks are completed; an administrator can close the issue.
statuses.closed: All tasks are closed — the issue is finished.

issues.list.title: Help — Issues

actions.label: Add issue
actions.text: Create an issue via the popup in the desktop version of Winprox or after scanning a QR code at a unit via the QR portal. A task is always automatically created which you can refine later on the Tasks page.

actions.label: Plan inspection round
actions.text: Separate flow next to Add issue: pick at least 2 stops (units), interval and team in one form. Creates a recurring issue with round stops and starts the first task immediately.

actions.label: Print briefing
actions.text: Print an overview of open tasks per team.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Combine status, team, search term, recurring and inspection rounds to refine the list. The search term looks in the description (source text and completed translations), location, address, postcode, city, unit and reporter. Press GO! to apply. Use the Inspection rounds filter (or sidebar Work → Inspection rounds) for recurring issues with at least two round stops.

actions.label: Approve
actions.text: Issues created via the QR portal wait for approval. Approve so content becomes visible on public pages.

issues.list.status_note: Issue status is derived automatically from the tasks on that issue.

statuses.new: New issue; at least one task has not been started yet.
statuses.in_progress: Follow-up is underway — a task has been started or is in progress.
statuses.done: All tasks have been completed by the team.
statuses.closed: An administrator has confirmed and closed everything.

issues.show.title: Help — Issue detail

actions.label: Add task
actions.text: Add a task to an existing issue or edit an existing task. Give a clear, concrete description of the problem or action to be performed (e.g., "Printer prints dirty"). Select a specific due date via the calendar. Leave this blank if the task should be picked up directly or flexibly. Determine the urgency of the task (Prio 1 to 3). This field is exclusive to administrators to prevent priority inflation on the shop floor. Assign the task to the right operational team. This team receives a direct notification. Workers start tasks via the unit QR portal after signing in via the Clock Point QR.

actions.label: Post update
actions.text: Add a note or photo to the issue; this will be shown on the portal.

actions.label: Approve
actions.text: Approve QR issues before description and photos become publicly visible.

actions.label: Description translation
actions.text: On approved issues, pick a language (NL, EN, FR, DE) next to the description. The text is translated automatically after approval by WinProx (periodically). If a translation is not ready yet, you will see «Not translated yet». Lists and search show the source text until then. Active announcements and documents follow the same pattern on the location page. Tasks with their own description show the translated text in lists and the portal once ready.

actions.label: Task translations
actions.text: In the task edit form you can manually update the task description per language (NL, EN, FR, DE). Useful when the automatic translation by WinProx (periodically) is wrong or still missing. Only available when the task has its own description. Saving finalises the translation for that language.

issues.show.status_note: Change issue status by updating the tasks.

statuses.new: Waiting for at least one task to start.
statuses.in_progress: At least one task is actively being worked on.
statuses.done: All tasks are completed; close the issue when everything is confirmed.

actions.label: Interval
actions.text: How often the issue recurs (e.g. every 2 weeks, every month, every quarter, every year).

actions.label: Lead (days)
actions.text: How many days before the due date the task is created (e.g. 7 days for monthly tasks).

actions.label: Inspection round stops
actions.text: Choose at least 2 units as stops (any locations; grouped by location). The list order is the round route order.

actions.label: Select all units
actions.text: Use the checkbox above the list to quickly select all units. You can then untick individual units if needed.

tasks.list.title: Help — Tasks

actions.label: Filter by team
actions.text: Show only tasks for one operational team. Team managers see only their teams by default.

actions.label: Open task
actions.text: Click a task for detail, status changes and the link to the issue.

actions.label: Recurring
actions.text: Filter recurring tasks (Recurring pill). These come from recurring issues with a planned due date per cycle.

tasks.list.status_note: Statuses are often updated automatically via the unit QR portal. You can also adjust them manually.

statuses.new: Task has been created and is waiting for the team to start.
statuses.in_progress: The team is working on it.
statuses.done: Work is finished by the worker; an administrator can close it.
statuses.closed: Task has been confirmed and closed.

tasks.show.title: Help — Task detail

actions.label: Recurring
actions.text: If the task comes from a recurring issue, you see the Recurring pill and this cycle's planned due date. A new cycle task is only created after the previous one is done or closed — so open tasks do not pile up.

actions.label: Inspection round
actions.text: For an inspection round you see progress per stop (OK, Not OK, skipped, open) with date/time and performer. On each stop unit QR portal the worker sees the same progress; the task completes automatically when all stops are done. You can also complete or close an open round here manually (with a reason when closing).

actions.label: Assign team
actions.text: Choose an operational team and save. You can also change an existing assignment.

actions.label: Change status
actions.text: Set the task to In progress, Completed or Closed depending on progress.

actions.label: Description translation
actions.text: If the task has its own description (not only the issue text), it is translated automatically by WinProx (periodically). In the task edit form you can manually update that description per language (NL, EN, FR, DE). Useful when the automatic translation is wrong or still missing. Saving finalises the translation for that language. Without its own description, the task follows the linked issue translation.

actions.label: Open issue
actions.text: Go to the linked issue for context, photos and additional tasks.

actions.label: Reading and follow-up
actions.text: Shown only on ESG measurement tasks. Lists the recorded value, any threshold alarm, the measurement task, and a follow-up task. Open on Reading goes to the filtered measurements overview; on Measurement task opens the linked task.

tasks.show.status_note: On the shop floor, workers start and complete tasks via the unit QR portal (after signing in via Clock Point QR).

statuses.done: Worker reports the work as done.

actions.label: Add location
actions.text: Create a new site with address and basic details.

actions.label: Open location
actions.text: Manage units, documents, announcements and QR codes per location.

actions.label: Show inactive
actions.text: Show deactivated locations to reactivate or review them.

actions.label: Location translations
actions.text: In the location edit form you can manually update the name per language (NL, EN, FR, DE). Useful when the automatic translation by WinProx (periodically) is wrong or still missing. Saving finalises the translation for that language.

actions.label: Categories
actions.text: Manage categories to group units (e.g. drills, plumbing, fitness equipment, office, electrical). Categories help with filtering and organizing units. By linking executor teams to specific categories, WinProx ensures that tasks can be carried out by the correct team. GPS location category: when "Allow GPS location" is checked, the GPS location of a unit can be submitted via the portal. This lets users of mobile units (e.g. crane, large machine) quickly communicate their location to administration.

actions.label: Category translations
actions.text: In the category edit form you can manually update the name per language (NL, EN, FR, DE). Useful when the automatic translation by WinProx (periodically) is wrong or still missing. Saving finalises the translation for that language.

actions.label: Reservable
actions.text: Turn on Reservable on a category for shared resources with a time slot (meeting room, vehicle, key, …). Then turn on Allow reservations per unit (off by default). The unit QR then shows the Reserve tile. Defect reports remain via Issue → task.

actions.label: Allow unit checks
actions.text: Turn on Allow unit checks on a category for quick OK/Not OK rounds (security, cleaning, …). Then turn on Allow unit checks per unit (off by default). Both must be on before workers see the Unit check tile on the unit QR. Separate from ESG measurements.

actions.label: Require contact details
actions.text: Turn this on if anonymous reporters via the unit QR must enter first name, last name and email. Off by default. Only takes effect when also enabled on the unit. Does not apply to signed-in field workers — they are already identified.

actions.label: Add unit
actions.text: Add an object/machine/asset/space with QR token and default team. A unit can be diverse: a machine, room, vehicle, aerial work platform, fitness device, etc. Set per unit whether visitors may submit reports.

actions.label: Location translations
actions.text: In the location edit form you can manually update the name per language (NL, EN, FR, DE). Useful when the automatic translation by WinProx (periodically) is wrong or still missing. Saving finalises the translation for that language.

actions.label: Unit translations
actions.text: In the unit edit form you can manually update name and description per language (NL, EN, FR, DE). Useful when the automatic translation by WinProx (periodically) is wrong or still missing. Saving finalises the translation for that language.

actions.label: Allow reservations
actions.text: Only relevant if the category is Reservable. Off by default; turn on to allow reservations for this unit. Other units in the same category stay independent.

actions.label: Allow unit checks
actions.text: Only relevant when the category allows unit checks. Off by default; turn on so workers can record OK/Not OK via the unit QR.

actions.label: External ID
actions.text: Only visible with API access (Corporate, or trial with API). Map the unit to your external facility software (IWMS, CMMS, ERP, …). External systems can then push unit checks via POST /api/v1/units/checks.

actions.label: Checklist (unit check)
actions.text: Optionally link a checklist to the unit (templates under the People → Teams page, shared or from the category’s teams). On Unit check in the portal the worker ticks each item before OK is saved.

actions.label: Require contact details
actions.text: Only relevant when the category requires this. Off by default. Applies only to anonymous QR reporters (first name, last name and email), not to workers signed in via Clock Point.

actions.label: Bulk units
actions.text: Create a range of units at once. Enter start number (as text so leading zeros are kept, e.g. 01 or 201), count, optional digits (padding; leave empty to auto-detect from the start number), prefix (e.g. Room + space) and suffix (e.g. -A). Examples: 01; Room 20–22; Room 201–203; Room 501. The preview lists names live; duplicates are highlighted in red and block Create. Optionally assign all new units to one category. Maximum 500 units per bulk.

actions.label: Import units
actions.text: Import units for this location via CSV or Excel (.xlsx). Required: unit_name. Optional: description, category_name. Location columns are not needed — everything goes on this location. If headers are wrong or required fields are missing, the entire import is rejected with a clear error per row. Categories are created automatically if they do not exist yet.

actions.label: Recent imports
actions.text: After an import, an overview of recent imports (30 days) for this location appears. Per import you see file name, date and unit count. Click Undo import to remove units without issues or tasks. Empty categories created only by the import are cleaned up. The location itself is kept.

actions.label: QR print sheet
actions.text: Download a Word file with QR stickers (Avery/HERMA) or full-page print sheets (A6/A5/A4, 1 QR per page) for all units at this location. You can also generate free dynamic QR codes that are not yet linked to a unit. These can first be attached to a unit and then assigned to a unit via the same QR code. Administrators/employees can link all units to these dynamic QR codes. Team workers can only link units that are connected to their team.

actions.label: GPS
actions.text: View a unit's location history via the pop-up once GPS coordinates are available. Click 'Open in Maps' to open the location directly in Google Maps.

actions.label: Documents & announcements
actions.text: Manage documents and announcements for the unit QR portal. Documents: turn on «Active» to publish in the portal. Without «Field workers only», any visitor can view and download the file. With «Field workers only», only a field worker signed in to the portal (name + icon) can see and download it — not via the admin screen with email login. Inactive documents remain visible only here. Active documents are translated automatically by WinProx (periodically; description); the edit form shows a translation preview per language. The title stays in the source language.

calendar.title: Help — Calendar

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Time overview of scheduled tasks, created issues and unit reservations. Admin screens show everything clearly — no blur here.

actions.label: View
actions.text: Choose month, week or day. Weeks start on Monday. Today is highlighted in emerald; days outside the selected month are grey.

actions.label: Navigation
actions.text: Browse with previous, today and next. The URL remembers view, type, date, location and (for reservations) category — useful to share or bookmark.

actions.label: Type
actions.text: Switch between Tasks (default), Issues and Reservations. Each type shows different items and status pills.

actions.label: Tasks
actions.text: Shows tasks with a planned date or due date — including cycles from recurring issues. Only tasks from approved issues. Sorted by priority. Click opens the task detail (reference number + status pill).

actions.label: Issues
actions.text: Shows issues on their creation date (when they came in). Click opens the issue detail.

actions.label: Reservations
actions.text: Shows active pending holds and confirmed bookings (cancelled or expired do not appear here). Per item: unit and time slot; in week and day view also the guest name. Click opens the reservations list.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Location: all locations or one. For Reservations a second filter appears for reservable categories. Switching back to Tasks or Issues clears that category filter.

actions.label: Month grid
actions.text: Up to five items per day; then «+X more». Use week or day view for the full list of that day.

actions.label: Week and day
actions.text: List cards per day. In day view, browse pages with previous/next when there are more than 50 items.

actions.label: Briefing
actions.text: Print briefing opens a printable overview of tasks for that day, grouped by team. In Tasks mode the briefing date follows the selected calendar day.

calendar.status_note: For Tasks and Issues, pills follow the task or issue status below. For Reservations: pending (awaiting email confirmation) or confirmed — those block overlapping slots.

statuses.new: Planned or new, not yet started.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Reservations are for shareable timed resources: meeting rooms, vehicles, keys, … Not for defect reports — those stay on Issue → task.

actions.label: Enable
actions.text: Turn on Reservable on the category. Then turn on Allow reservations per unit (off by default). The unit QR then shows the Reserve tile.

actions.label: Guest flow
actions.text: A guest books via QR, gets a 30-minute hold and confirms by email. Change or cancel via the mail link or again via QR (name/email remembered in a cookie).

actions.label: Admin
actions.text: Here you create immediately confirmed reservations, edit time slots and cancel bookings. Filters: upcoming, pending, confirmed, past. Open the calendar for the time-block overview.

actions.label: Overlap
actions.text: The system blocks overlapping slots for confirmed and active pending holds. Expired pending holds lapse after 30 minutes.

actions.label: Colleague users
actions.text: Manage administrative staff who primarily work on a PC. They must log in with email and password. An administrator is the main user who can update company details. The administrator can add other administrators and staff members depending on the chosen subscription.

actions.label: Print briefing
actions.text: Open a printable overview of open tasks per team — useful on the shop floor. The same briefing is also available on Dashboard, Issues and Calendar.

actions.label: Operational teams
actions.text: Create teams and workers, assign team leaders. A unit must have a team linked so that a worker can handle tasks for this unit. As long as there are no workers in the team, you can still delete the team.

actions.label: Checklists
actions.text: Create checklists under the People → Teams page (optionally per team or shared). Optionally copy a starter (cleaning, technical, security). Then link them per unit via Locations → edit unit. Only checklists of teams linked to the category (or shared) appear in the dropdown. Points must be checked before OK. After saving, WinProx automatically translates the name and items into the other languages (Ollama); editing the source language queues translations again.

actions.label: Team translations
actions.text: In the team edit form you can manually update the name per language (NL, EN, FR, DE). Useful when the automatic translation by WinProx (periodically) is wrong or still missing. Saving finalises the translation for that language.

actions.label: Clock Point QR code
actions.text: The Clock Point QR is the printable QR that workers use to sign in (name + icon) and clock in or out. Manage and print it under Time → Clock Points.

actions.label: Workers
actions.text: Workers have no email login; they sign in via the Clock Point QR with name and icon. You can also add their email address and phone number.

actions.label: External workers
actions.text: When adding or editing a worker, tick External worker for installers, painters, freelancers or other external staff. You can then optionally enter a company name (e.g. BrightSpark Electrical). In the list they show an Ext badge and the company name if set. They use the same Clock Point and unit-QR flow as internal workers — no separate portal or login.

actions.label: Sort order
actions.text: Determine the order in which teams appear in lists and dropdowns. Lower numbers appear first.

actions.label: How long do workers stay logged in?
actions.text: Choose how long a worker stays logged in after scanning the Clock Point QR: Daily (14 hours), Weekly (144 hours, 6 working days) or Custom (custom number of hours). The default value is 14 hours.

actions.label: Reset icon
actions.text: Remove the chosen icon from a worker so they can sign in again with a different icon. Useful if a worker wants to change icon or if an icon was selected by mistake. Team leaders can also remove icons from their team members in their portal.

actions.label: Deactivate team
actions.text: Disable a team so it is no longer visible in dropdowns and lists. Workers from this team can no longer view or complete tasks. Reactivation is possible.

actions.label: Deactivate worker
actions.text: Disable a worker so they can no longer sign in via Clock Point QR. The worker remains in the system and can be reactivated later.

actions.label: Delete worker
actions.text: Permanently remove a worker from the system. All history and tasks for this worker are preserved, but the worker can no longer be used.

actions.label: Import
actions.text: Import workers in bulk via CSV or Excel (.xlsx). The file must have exactly these headers: team_name, first_name, last_name (required), email, phone, company_name (optional). A filled company name automatically marks the worker as external. If the headers do not match or required fields are missing, the entire import is rejected with a clear error message per row. Teams are automatically created if they do not exist yet. Undo removes workers without a linked device and cleans up empty teams created by the import. Workers linked to a device (worker_device) are always kept.

actions.label: Recent imports
actions.text: After an import, an overview of the last 10 imports (30 days) appears automatically. Per import you see the file name, date and number of workers. Click Undo import to remove the workers of that batch. Only workers without a linked device are deleted — workers who are already signed in via Clock Point QR (and thus have an active device) remain and are marked as «Has devices». The button disappears once all workers in a batch have been deleted.

actions.label: Configuration overview
actions.text: At the very top you will find a collapsible overview of your environment's configuration status. Expand it to see the completeness meter, eight counts (inactive locations, units, teams and workers; categories with or without GPS; active and inactive documents) and the most important action items with a direct Fix link. If the panel shows a badge, there are open action items. Use Open full overview to go to the dedicated configuration page with all action items and filter cards per type.

actions.label: Organisation details
actions.text: Only the administrator can change name, email, phone and address via 'Edit organisation details'. These details appear on printed QR stickers, unit labels and other reporter-facing material.

actions.label: Organisation logo
actions.text: The administrator uploads an organisation logo (PNG/JPG, max. 2 MB). As an employee you only see the current logo for reference. It appears in the centre of every QR code on stickers and in the reporting portal. For corner placement on stickers, see the Logo and address section under QR sticker sheets.

actions.label: Portal background
actions.text: Optional background image for the reporting portal after scanning a QR code (PNG/JPG, max. 4 MB). This is not the same as the sticker background under QR sticker sheets.

actions.label: WinProx style
actions.text: Choose how WinProx looks for you in admin: Standard or Dark. Your choice applies on all devices where you are signed in.

actions.label: Custom portal style
actions.text: Turn on 'Use custom portal style' to choose background and button colours for the reporting portal. The preview card shows how reporters see the portal after a scan. This does not affect the admin interface.

actions.label: QR print sheet
actions.text: Branding for printed Avery 62×89-R stickers (9 labels per sheet). Download the sticker sheet per location from the QR pack.

actions.label: Text
actions.text: Your custom text appears at the top of the sticker (max. 120 characters). If left empty, WinProx uses location name · unit automatically. The sticker number always appears below the QR code. The preview on the right updates live. Click 'Save' to store text (and logo settings).

actions.label: Logo and address
actions.text: Choose where your organisation logo appears on the sticker (bottom right, bottom left, …) — only if you have uploaded a logo. Tick 'Show location address on sticker' to print address details at the bottom left. Address and bottom logo share one full-width white band at the bottom of the sticker; at the top each element stays separate. The logo in the centre of the QR code is fixed (your logo or WinProx) and cannot be moved here.

actions.label: Background
actions.text: Pick a custom image (PNG/JPG, max. 4 MB); it is saved immediately. Without a custom background WinProx uses the default sticker design. Use 'Remove custom background' to return to that default.

actions.label: Preview
actions.text: On the right (on a wide screen) you see a live preview of one sticker with a demo QR code and number. When exporting at a location, the real unit QR codes and sticker numbers for that location are used.

actions.label: Privacy & data export
actions.text: Only the administrator can download a machine-readable overview (JSON) of the account and relevant activity within your environment. This section appears on Settings for administrators only. The file may contain sensitive data — keep it secure.

actions.label: What is this page?
actions.text: Here you connect WinProx to other software — for example your ERP, a planning tool or a custom dashboard. WinProx then talks to that system digitally, so you do not have to retype issues manually.

actions.label: Do I need this?
actions.text:
Usually not. If you only use WinProx via the website and QR codes, you do not need to configure anything here.

For one-off setup: Want to import thousands of units or workers at once? Use the CSV/Excel import on a location (units) or on Teams (workers). That is often faster and simpler for an initial migration.

For ongoing automation: This API page is intended for administrators or IT partners who want to build a live integration so systems communicate automatically (e.g. real-time ERP connections or custom dashboards).

actions.label: API — what is it?
actions.text: An API lets other programs read WinProx data or perform actions (e.g. list issues and tasks). This works securely with an API token — like a password used by software, not by people.

actions.label: Creating an API token
actions.text: Give the token a clear name (e.g. "ERP integration"). After creation you see the code once: copy and store it immediately. WinProx will not show it again. If you lose it, create a new token and revoke the old one.

actions.label: Revoking a token
actions.text: No longer using an integration, or worried a token was exposed? Click Revoke. That integration stops working. Other tokens stay active.

actions.label: What can the API do?
actions.text: With a valid token, software can among other things read issues and tasks, list locations/units/teams/workers, create or approve issues, and start or complete tasks. For technical docs, ask your IT partner or WinProx support.

actions.label: Webhooks — what are they?
actions.text: A webhook is the opposite of the API: WinProx sends a message to your system when something happens (e.g. new issue or task completed). You provide a URL where WinProx may post data.

actions.label: Adding a webhook endpoint
actions.text: Enter a full URL starting with https:// (secure connection). Tick the events you want to receive. Optionally add a description (e.g. "Production ERP"). Save — WinProx stores the address and sends data automatically for those events.

actions.label: Event: issue.created
actions.text: A new issue was received (via QR, manually or via the API). Useful to create a ticket in an external system right away.

actions.label: Event: issue.approved
actions.text: An administrator approved an issue (often from QR). Only then is the content also visible on public QR pages.

actions.label: Event: issue.status_changed
actions.text: An issue's status changed (e.g. from open to in progress), usually because tasks were started or completed.

actions.label: Event: task.created
actions.text: A new task was created for a team, linked to an issue.

actions.label: Event: task.started
actions.text: A worker started a task via the field portal (unit QR).

actions.label: Event: task.completed
actions.text: A task was completed by the team. Useful to update external systems or reports.

actions.label: Event: unit.gps_reported
actions.text: A GPS location was recorded for a unit via the portal (reporter, worker or admin during QR linking). Payload includes coordinates and optionally location_name and country_code (GeoNames).

actions.label: Endpoint active or inactive
actions.text: Temporarily turn off an endpoint without deleting it (e.g. during server maintenance). Inactive endpoints receive no messages.

actions.label: Recent deliveries
actions.text: Log of the latest webhook attempts. "success" means your system received the message. "failed" means something went wrong (wrong URL, server offline, …). Shows delivery status only — not issue content.

actions.label: Security
actions.text: Treat API tokens like passwords: do not share them in email or chat. Webhooks are cryptographically signed so your server can verify the message really came from WinProx — your IT partner can implement this check.

actions.label: Help with the integration
actions.text: Not sure if something works? Ask your IT partner to check the URL, events and recent deliveries. For WinProx itself, use Contact or the FAQ if you do not have a developer.

actions.label: Trial period
actions.text: During the trial you have extended limits. The dashboard shows remaining days.

actions.label: Choose plan
actions.text: Select a plan that fits the number of units you manage.

actions.label: Delete organisation data
actions.text: Administrators only. First download a data export via Settings → Privacy & data export. Then on Subscription tick the confirmation and enter your password. All administrators receive a confirmation email. During a trial you can then permanently delete yourself (technical snapshot without media, kept 30 days). On a paid plan there is a 7-day wait with banner and reminder email; WinProx administration performs the deletion. You can cancel until then via Subscription. If the trial ends without a subscription, warning emails follow and the organisation may be deleted automatically (default around day 14).

actions.label: Knowledge base
actions.text: Answers to frequently asked questions about WinProx, QR, teams, Time, ESG, portal approval/blur, and page help (?).

actions.label: Support
actions.text: Contact WinProx if you need help beyond this page help and the FAQ.

portal.worker.qr.title: Help — QR codes on the shop floor

actions.label: Unit QR
actions.text: Attached to a machine, room or asset. Citizens can report issues here. As a worker, sign in first via the Clock Point QR; then scan the unit QR to start or complete open tasks on that unit. When unit checks are enabled, signed-in workers can also record OK/Not OK (with an optional checklist).

actions.label: Clock Point QR
actions.text: Placed at the entrance, warehouse or workshop. Workers sign in here (name + icon) and clock in and out. They can then handle tasks via unit QR codes.

portal.unit.title: Help — Public portal

actions.label: Welcome
actions.text: Welcome to the public portal of :tenant. Read below for more information. Interested in your own company portal? Click on Winprox.app.

actions.label: Report issue
actions.text: Tap "Create report", describe the problem and optionally add up to four photos. First name, last name and email are optional — unless the administrator made contact details required; then fill them in. A task is then created for the team. The report must be approved before it appears on the portal. Anti-spam limits apply: at most one report per 3 minutes and five reports per 30 minutes for this unit (per device).

actions.label: Reserve
actions.text: If this unit is reservable, you see the Reserve tile. Pick a time slot, enter name and email, and confirm within 30 minutes via email. Use My reservations or the mail link to change or cancel.

actions.label: Documents
actions.text: View the manuals and other documents available for this unit here. Pick a language at the top — the description is translated automatically once ready.

actions.label: Announcements
actions.text: View the announcements that apply specifically to this unit here. Pick a language at the top — the text is translated automatically once ready.

actions.label: Capture GPS location
actions.text: When enabled, your GPS coordinates are shared with the administration. This helps a technician find you easily.

actions.label: Language
actions.text: Choose your desired language in the top right (NL, EN, DE, FR). The texts on the portal are immediately updated to the chosen language.

actions.label: Theme
actions.text: Switch between Standard and Dark themes in the top right for a view that matches your preference. Dark is useful on mobile.

portal.unit.status_note: Open tasks on this page follow the statuses below.

actions.label: Add photos
actions.text: When starting or completing a task, add photos as proof or explanation. Photos are automatically compressed for fast upload.

actions.label: Wait for upload
actions.text: Wait until the upload finishes before confirming — otherwise photos will be missing from the task.

portal.team.title: Help — Worker portal

actions.label: Name and icon
actions.text: After scanning the Clock Point QR, enter your first and last name and choose a personal icon. Remember this icon well, because next time you must select it again. You get two attempts to sign in with the correct icon; after that your account is blocked. A team leader or administrator can unblock your account in that case.

actions.label: First time
actions.text: New to the team? Ask your team leader or administrator to create an account for you. After that you can sign in with your first and last name and choose your own icon.

actions.label: Sign out
actions.text: Sign out when you are finished. At times set by the administrator you are also automatically signed out.

actions.label: Open tasks
actions.text: After signing in via Clock Point QR you see open tasks for your team on the unit portal. Scan the unit QR on site to start or complete a task.

actions.label: New team tasks
actions.text: If new tasks for your team arrived since you signed in via Clock Point, the unit portal shows a sticky attention banner. Open the task overview via the Clock Point link or dismiss the banner.

actions.label: Start
actions.text: Go to "Open tasks" and click on "Start task". Other team members will then see that you are working on this task and the status changes to "In progress". Once you are finished, click on "Complete task".

actions.label: Complete
actions.text: After you have started the task, complete it by clicking on "Complete task". Here you can add a short note and optionally attach photos. Sometimes the portal asks for a measurement value (e.g. a meter reading) — enter it before you confirm. The task then gets status "Completed".

actions.label: Unit check
actions.text: When category and unit both allow unit checks, signed-in workers see the Unit check tile. Record OK or Not OK, optionally with a checklist. OK does not create an issue; after Not OK you can create a report.

actions.label: Capture GPS location
actions.text: When enabled, your GPS coordinates are shared with the administration. This helps a technician find you easily.

portal.team.status_note: Each task goes through the statuses below:

statuses.new: The task is not yet started and waiting for a worker.
statuses.in_progress: Someone is currently working on the task on site.
statuses.done: The work has been completed by a worker.
statuses.closed: The issue has been checked by the administrator and definitively closed.

actions.label: Role
actions.text: A team leader is a worker with extra rights on the team portal. You handle tasks yourself and help colleagues get started.

actions.label: Assignment
actions.text: An administrator assigns team leaders in WinProx on the team. You see the «Team leader» badge after signing in.

actions.label: Clock Point QR
actions.text: Scan the Clock Point QR and sign in with your name and icon — the same as any worker.

actions.label: Extra panels
actions.text: After signing in you see extra sections: release colleague icon and manage workers.

actions.label: When needed
actions.text: If a colleague picked the wrong icon too often, they are blocked. You can release the icon so they can choose again.

actions.label: Steps
actions.text: Open «Release», confirm your own icon first, select the blocked colleague and confirm. The colleague can then sign in again.

actions.label: Overview
actions.text: Open «Manage» to see all workers on your team, including the team leader badge.

actions.label: Add
actions.text: Add a new worker with first and last name. Then let the colleague scan the Clock Point QR to register and choose an icon.

actions.label: Remove
actions.text: Remove workers who no longer belong to the team. You cannot remove yourself.

portal.teamleader.tasks.title: Help — Handle tasks

actions.label: Same as worker
actions.text: Start open tasks, add notes, attach photos and complete — identical to the workers manual.

actions.label: Coordination
actions.text: Keep overview of open tasks and coordinate who picks up which task with your team.

portal.teamleader.tasks.status_note: Task statuses are the same as for all workers.

statuses.done: Completed by you or a colleague.

actions.label: Sign in
actions.text: Scan the Clock Point QR sticker and sign in with your first and last name and your personal icon. Two wrong attempts temporarily block your account — a team leader or administrator can release it.

actions.label: Open tasks
actions.text: After signing in you see a read-only overview of open tasks for your team. To start or complete a task, scan the unit QR on site.

actions.label: Clock in and out
actions.text: Clock in, out and register breaks here. Then use the unit QR on site to start or complete tasks.

actions.label: Sign out
actions.text: Sign out when you are finished. At times set by the administrator you are also automatically signed out.

actions.label: What gets translated?
actions.text: Automatic translation slots (NL, EN, FR, DE) for: approved QR issues (description); active announcements (description); active units (name and description); tasks with their own description; active documents (description — title stays in source language). Tasks without their own description show the linked issue translation.

actions.label: Local via Ollama
actions.text: As superuser on your laptop: start php artisan queue:work, click « Start translations ». Pending issues, announcements, units, tasks and documents are exported, translated locally, and imported back on the server.

actions.label: Server status
actions.text: On production you see how many translations are still waiting. The count includes all of these types.

actions.label: Source text changed
actions.text: If someone edits the source text of an announcement, unit, task or document, existing translations are invalidated and set to pending again. Run a new translation sync afterwards.

actions.label: Manage tenants
actions.text: Overview of all organisations. Open a tenant to work in their environment as support.

actions.label: Support mode
actions.text: Start support to use the app on behalf of a tenant. Stop support to return to the platform overview.

actions.label: Modules
actions.text: Enable or disable optional modules (ESG, IoT Connect). Time (hours, presence and Clock Points) is included with every subscription by default.

actions.label: Unanswered questions
actions.text: Questions from the help chat with no FAQ match. Answer them or add them to the knowledge base.

actions.label: Knowledge base
actions.text: Manage FAQ articles and help answers for all tenants.

actions.label: What is this screen?
actions.text: Manage addresses that no longer receive WinProx emails — marketing, contact and system mail. Only superusers see this page.

actions.label: Block an address
actions.text: Add an email address manually to block it. That row gets the source Blocked manually.

actions.label: Search and filter
actions.text: Search by email address. By default (checkbox off) bounce addresses are hidden. Turn on Undeliverable (bounce) to show only addresses blocked automatically after a failed promo email; the count is in parentheses.

actions.label: Unsubscribe source
actions.text: Unsubscribed by recipient = via the unsubscribe link in an email. Undeliverable (bounce) = automatic after an undeliverable promo email. Blocked manually = via this screen.

actions.label: Restore
actions.text: Restore removes the address from the list; it will receive emails again.

actions.label: What is this screen?
actions.text: The ESG dashboard gives an operational overview of your measurement programme: latest values, threshold alarms, trends, and open follow-up actions. It is your starting point for day-to-day ESG management — detail and history are on the Measurements tab.

actions.label: KPI cards at the top
actions.text: The first card shows the number of threshold alarms in the recent sample. You also see the latest reading per active numeric indicator and when it was recorded. Highlighted in red = outside minimum or maximum. Click a card to open the filtered measurements overview.

actions.label: Usage trend
actions.text: Line chart for the selected indicator over the last 30 days. Readings per day are summed (useful for consumption indicators such as kWh). Choose another indicator at the top right to compare trends.

actions.label: Readings within limits
actions.text: The donut shows the percentage of recent readings (sample) that fall within the configured thresholds. The caption below states how many alarms are in that sample. Click to open the measurements overview.

actions.label: Highest usage per location
actions.text: Ranking of locations by the total sum of readings for the selected indicator in the last 30 days. Useful to see which building or site contributes most. Click a row for readings at that location.

actions.label: ESG score (compliance)
actions.text: Weighted score over the last 30 days: 60% threshold compliance (readings with thresholds that are within limits) + 40% measurement coverage (active numeric indicators with at least one reading). Below the donut you see the individual percentages.

actions.label: Distribution by category
actions.text: Donut of the number of readings per indicator category (e.g. energy, waste, safety) in the last 30 days. Set categories when creating or editing an indicator under Indicators.

actions.label: Open ESG tasks
actions.text: Tasks linked to an ESG indicator that are not yet completed — both periodic measurement tasks and automatic follow-up actions. The Auto-alarm badge marks tasks WinProx created after a threshold breach.

actions.label: Auto-alarm and follow-up task
actions.text: When a reading falls outside the configured minimum or maximum, WinProx can automatically create a priority-2 follow-up task (at most one open task per indicator and unit). The Follow-up task button on recent readings and alarms goes straight to that task. The assigned team follows the team of the original measurement task.

actions.label: Recent readings and threshold alarms
actions.text: Two lists at the bottom: all recent readings, and separately readings with threshold alarms. Values outside limits get the Outside thresholds label. Use Task to open the measurement task from the QR portal.

actions.label: Empty dashboard
actions.text: No indicators or readings yet? WinProx shows getting-started steps: module active, create an indicator, link to a recurring issue. Full guidance on indicators is on the Indicators tab.

actions.label: How does it work?
actions.text: The ESG module lets you collect data systematically on site — energy use, safety checks, waste logging — without asking workers to do anything special. They simply see a task, as usual.

actions.label: Enable module
actions.text: A superuser must first enable the ESG module under Platform → Tenants. Without it, this menu is hidden.

actions.label: Step 1 — Create an indicator
actions.text: An indicator describes what you want to measure: an electricity meter, a fire extinguisher check, or a periodic inspection. Give it a clear name and, for numbers, a unit (e.g. kWh, m³) so it displays correctly at entry.

actions.label: Number
actions.text: For meter readings or counts (e.g. electricity in kWh, water in m³, vehicle mileage). You can set a minimum and maximum so unrealistic entries (e.g. a negative reading) are flagged.

actions.label: Yes/No
actions.text: For quick checks (e.g. "Is the emergency exit clear?", "Is the fire extinguisher inspected?").

actions.label: Text
actions.text: For a short note or comment with a reading (e.g. a remark about an unusual meter value).

actions.label: Choice list
actions.text: For a fixed set of answers (e.g. waste category: General waste, Recyclables, Paper). You define the options when creating the indicator; workers choose from a dropdown on the portal.

actions.label: Linked system
actions.text: When values come in automatically from an external system (via the API). Not intended for manual entry by workers on the QR portal.

actions.label: Step 2 — Link to a recurring issue
actions.text: When creating a recurring issue on a unit, you can link an ESG indicator. From then on, each cycle automatically asks for the corresponding reading — for example the monthly meter reading for that unit.

actions.label: Step 3 — Measurements are stored
actions.text:
Each time a worker completes the task, the entered value is stored with the date and unit. This gradually builds a history per measurement point, useful for reporting (e.g. energy use per building over time).

Once recorded, a measurement cannot be changed — this keeps your data reliable and auditable. The overview is on the Measurements tab.

actions.label: Deactivate indicator
actions.text: No longer using an indicator (e.g. a replaced meter)? Deactivate it instead of deleting. All collected measurements remain fully preserved — you never lose historical data.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: History of all ESG readings on one unit: trend, timeline, and alarms per indicator.

actions.label: Reading and follow-up
actions.text: Under each reading in the timeline you see linked steps: the reading (value), optionally a threshold alarm, the measurement task used to enter the value, and a follow-up task when the value was outside limits. Use Open to jump to the measurements overview or the task.

actions.label: Trend
actions.text: Chart of numeric readings over the recent period for the selected indicator.

actions.label: What do you see here?
actions.text: All readings workers entered when completing a task, with indicator, location, unit, timestamp, and who took the reading. Click Task to view the underlying work item.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Narrow by indicator, location, unit, or period. Useful to review all meter readings for one building in a quarter, for example.

actions.label: Threshold warnings
actions.text: If an indicator has a minimum or maximum set, readings outside those limits are highlighted so you spot deviations quickly.

actions.label: External integration
actions.text: Readings can also arrive automatically via an API connection (Settings → API). This is optional — most organisations collect data through the unit QR portal.

actions.label: Dashboard
actions.text: Live KPIs at the top: clocked in, active, break, not clocked in, and attention. Click a tile to filter. Attention opens the alarms screen.

actions.label: Views
actions.text: Choose Teams (accordion), Team cards (summary per team), or Locations (clocked in per site). Expand a team only when you need worker details.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Filter by team, location, clock point, or search by name. Status filters: present, break, or absent.

actions.label: Close shift
actions.text: Close an open shift at the current time when someone forgot to clock out. The reason is recorded in the audit log.

actions.label: Clock Point QR
actions.text: Workers clock in and out via the QR sticker on a clock point (/time/…). Identification uses name and icon — no separate login.

actions.label: Purpose
actions.text: Shows open shifts that need attention: clocked in too long, forgotten clock-out, or no break recorded.

actions.label: Types
actions.text: Filter by Long shift (>10 h), Not clocked out (>16 h), or No break (>6 h without a break).

actions.label: Action
actions.text: Use Close shift to end a shift with a reason. The nav badge shows the total alarm count.

actions.label: Period and filters
actions.text: Choose from and to dates and optionally filter by team, worker, or clock point. Click Apply to refresh the list.

actions.label: Export CSV
actions.text: Download filtered shifts as CSV (Excel-friendly, semicolon-separated). Ideal for payroll or planning tools.

actions.label: Print
actions.text: Open a printable timesheet with the same filters. Use browser Print to save or share as PDF.

actions.label: Correct
actions.text: For closed shifts, an admin can adjust clock-in/out times or break minutes with a required reason. Changes are recorded in the audit log.

actions.label: Close shift
actions.text: Open shifts in this overview can also be force-closed, same as on the Presence screen.

actions.label: Statuses
actions.text: Open — still clocked in. Closed — clocked out normally. Closed (admin) — manually closed by admin. Closed (automatic) — system closed a forgotten shift after the threshold.

actions.label: Link tasks
actions.text: Start or complete a task via the unit QR portal while clocked in — the task is automatically linked to the open shift. Open links are closed on clock-out.

actions.label: What is a clock point?
actions.text: Manage clock-in points and printable QR codes under Time → Clock Points. A default clock point is created automatically if needed.

actions.label: Print QR code
actions.text: Use QR code to open a quick browser print page. Click Print and place the QR at the entrance, warehouse, or other location. Each clock point has a unique code.

actions.label: QR print sheet
actions.text: Use QR print sheet to download a Word file with one full-page QR (A6, A5 or A4) for this clock point. The sheet uses the same background and branding as Settings → QR print sheet (A6/A5/A4).

actions.label: Renew QR code
actions.text: Generate a new QR when a sticker is lost or you suspect misuse. The old code still works for a few days (grace period), then it is blocked.

actions.label: QR rotation
actions.text: Set an interval (months). The system recommends renewal at a random moment within that interval. Until you renew, clocking in still works — it is a recommendation, not a block.

actions.label: Blocked scans
actions.text: When someone uses an expired QR, access is denied and logged. A warning appears here if there were blocked attempts in the last 7 days.

actions.label: Active / inactive
actions.text: Deactivate a clock point temporarily (e.g. during off-site work). The portal then shows that clock-in is unavailable.

actions.label: Documents
actions.text: Privacy policy, terms of service and other legal texts from WinProx.

actions.label: What is this screen?
actions.text: This is WinProx’s activity log: who did what, when, and in which organisation. Plain language instead of technical codes.

actions.label: Reading a row
actions.text: The bold line is the event. After it: organisation, person (or System) and time. Extra context (name, email, file, #id) appears underneath when available.

actions.label: Search
actions.text: Search by everyday words (e.g. issue, promo), organisation name, or the user’s name/email.

actions.label: Why it helps
actions.text: Useful to see who approved an issue, which promo campaign was imported, or who unsubscribed — without digging into the database.

actions.label: What is this screen?
actions.text: Manage gateways, sensors, alarm rules and review recent events. WinProx receives sensor events; physical sensors and protocols stay with your gateway/vendor.

actions.label: Facility vs Corporate
actions.text: Facility: alarms become approved issues with tasks. Corporate: the same, plus sensor measurements into ESG when the sensor has a unit and numeric ESG indicator.

actions.label: Edit
actions.text: You can edit or deactivate gateways, sensors and rules later. For a gateway you can also rotate the token (the old token then stops working). We do not hard-delete: events are kept.

actions.label: What is a gateway?
actions.text: A gateway is the bridge between your sensors and WinProx. Sensors often talk to a vendor gateway over LoRaWAN, Zigbee, Bluetooth or MQTT. That gateway translates the data and forwards only relevant events to WinProx (over HTTPS). WinProx does not sell sensors or gateways: here you register a logical gateway with a token so WinProx knows which organisation may receive the events.

actions.label: Create a gateway
actions.text: Create a gateway and save the token immediately — it is shown only once. Configure it in your IoT gateway (X-WinProx-Iot-Key or Bearer).

actions.label: Sensors
actions.text: Map an external sensor ID (as sent by the gateway) to a name, type and preferably a unit. For ESG measurements (Corporate), also link an active numeric ESG indicator.

actions.label: Alarm rules
actions.text: A rule decides when an event becomes an issue: operator + threshold, issue text, team and priority. While an open task exists for the same rule, new alarms are deduplicated.

actions.label: Sending events
actions.text: The gateway posts to POST /api/v1/iot/events with kind alarm or measurement. Optional: idempotency_key to avoid duplicate posts. See the API docs (IoT Connect).

actions.label: Enable
actions.text: Turn on Allow unit checks on the category, then per unit (off by default). Only then does Unit check appear on the portal for signed-in workers.

actions.label: Checklists
actions.text: Create checklists under the People → Teams page (optionally per team or shared). Optionally copy a starter (cleaning, technical, security). Then link them per unit via Locations → edit unit. Only checklists of teams linked to the category (or shared) appear in the dropdown. Points must be checked before OK. After saving, WinProx automatically translates the name and items into the other languages (Ollama); editing the source language queues translations again.

actions.label: Starters
actions.text: Under the People → Teams → Checklists section you can copy a template (cleaning, technical, security) and then adjust it. Afterwards link the checklist per unit.

actions.label: OK and open tasks
actions.text: OK only stores the check (no issue). Not OK stores the check; the worker can then create a normal report. Open tasks remain separate on the portal.

actions.label: What is a unit check?
actions.text: A quick confirmation on the unit QR: OK or Not OK, with worker, timestamp and optional GPS. OK does not create an issue.

actions.label: Not OK
actions.text: Not OK stores the check and then lets the worker create a normal report via the portal.

actions.label: Filters
actions.text: Filter by result (OK / Not OK) and location. Open GPS to view coordinates on a map.

actions.label: Webhooks
actions.text: Each check triggers unit.check.recorded so external systems (IWMS, CMMS, ERP, …) can update the round.

actions.label: Inbound API
actions.text: External systems push checks with external_unit_id (the unit's External ID). Optional external_id on the check for idempotent retries. See Unit Checks API docs.

actions.label: Overview
actions.text: Tenant-wide list of all units: name, location, category and whether unit checks are allowed. Open a row to jump to the location detail with that unit in focus.

actions.label: Filter by location
actions.text: Narrow the list to one location. Clear the filter to see all units again.

actions.label: Unit checks
actions.text: The pills show Active/Inactive and whether unit checks are allowed (category and unit both on). Configure checks under Places → Categories / Locations, and checklists under People → Teams.
